messages:
carol: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about a minimal "bridge" adapter that lets SDKs fall back from streaming to paged calls when transport doesn't support resume. Short thread to align on ergonomics.

bob: +1. Are we aiming for identical return types across runtimes? that's the hard bit.

alice: Prefer same logical iterator in Python/TS/Go, but impl can vary. surface should expose async iterator (ts/py) and channel/iterator in go.

dave: Concern: retries. If we switch from stream->paged mid-stream, how do we surface idempotency? need resume token semantics.

carol: Agree. Proposal: adapter returns an opaque "continuation" token when switching. SDKs treat it as a cursor; not user-parsable. keeps semantics stable.

eva: Sounds good. For py/ts: iterator yields items and may yield a special 'checkpoint' object with token. Users rarely touch it.

frank: For Go, return (Item, Continuation) on each Next? that feels verbose.

alice: Alternative: keep Next() returning item and have Iterator.Continue() to pull token if needed. but then race with concurrent consumers.

bob: Simpler: make adapter manage concurrency — documented as not safe for concurrent iteration; keep surface minimal.

dave: Back to retries: on partial failure after switch, adapter should be able to reconstitute the paged cursor and retry idempotently. That means we need server support to accept continuation tokens.

carol: Server-side already emits opaque pagination tokens for many endpoints. We'll extend to include stream-offset metadata. product ok with that?

eva: I'll sync with backend team. From SDK side: we should expose config: {fallback: 'auto'|'never', max_items_before_fallback: int}

bob: +1 for config. Also need telemetry events: fallback.triggered, fallback.reason, resume.success.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: note: canary for pagination-token change in staging scheduled for Wed 02:00 UTC :bell:

frank: Docs note: show example for ts/py/golang. tiny snippets.

alice: Example for TS:

```ts
for await (const item of client.listWidgets({limit:50}, {fallback:'auto'})) {
  // handle item
}
```

carol: Example for Python similar. For Go provide Next() loop example.

dave: Edgecase: what if user supplied a per-call timeout? fallback may increase RPCs and latency. config should allow 'prefer_low_latency'.

carol: Good call. Add option fallback.strategy = 'latency'|'throughput'. Default 'throughput'.

eva: OK I'll draft a short RFC addendum with API sketches and telemetry. target: end of week.

bob: Thanks. If no objections, we'll land the SDK surface proposal and start mocks.

alice: No objections from me.

frank: 👍

carol: Thanks everyone. Filing follow-up action items in the RFC thread.
